subject: skill/stack/web-svg-css
claim: Build inline SVG through the SVG namespace — document.createElementNS("http://www.w3.org/2000/svg", ...) — and keep geometry on the node (viewBox, rx, points) rather than relying on CSS, because SVG is XML with its own namespace rules; the Control Room's burn trace and sparklines already do this. Style with the CSS cascade/specificity and inheritance, custom properties, and flex/grid layout. Meet WCAG contrast: at least 4.5:1 for normal text, 3:1 for large text (18pt or 14pt bold), 7:1 for enhanced text, and 3:1 for non-text UI/graphical objects; never rely on color alone, and give meaningful graphics a text alternative or ARIA label.
notes: SVG backs the XML/namespace nature and the CSS/DOM/JavaScript integration. CSS backs cascade, specificity, inheritance, custom properties, flexbox and grid. WCAG Perceivable backs the exact contrast thresholds (1.4.3, 1.4.6, 1.4.11), the use-of-color rule (1.4.1) and text alternatives (1.1.1). All three agree; uncertainty is modest because the CSS source fetched largely as an index/subsection list. The createElementNS/viewBox/aria pattern is the repo's own (apps/control_room/static/app.js).
